notes:
Summary: priority is deterministic throughput for auction-time scoring. Heavy tail token distribution (20% of requests are 1-20 tokens, 5% > 512 tokens). Key ask: a minimum sustained tokens/sec guarantee to avoid bid timeouts during peak events; clear concurrency caps so their match engine can provision upstream.

Throughput / SLA specifics discussed:
- Customer requests min baseline 120k tokens/sec sustained for dedicated pool (measured at model output tokens).
- Concurrency cap proposal: 1,000 concurrent requests for the primary model (gptx-emu-16k), with soft burst to 3,000 for 15 minutes once per 24h.
- Burst policy: 3-tier approach: immediate burst credit (token-bucket) up to 3x baseline for 15 minutes, automated graceful fallback to smaller quantized variant (gptx-emu-8q) after burst threshold, and region-failover to secondary capacity in eu-west if local pool exhausted.
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms for requests < 64 tokens; p99 target 300ms with explicit carved-out allowance for cold-KV cache events.
- Measurement and reporting: token/sec and concurrency measured at ingress and egress; monthly SLA report and realtime dashboard hooks (console API).
- Penalties: negotiating credits model (pro-rated reserved capacity credit) vs. service credits; legal prefers credits tied to minutes below min tokens/sec over a rolling 1-hour window.

Technical notes / constraints:
- Preferred HW: H100 80GB preferred, fallback to A100 80GB with documented performance delta. Need reserved pool sizing guidance from Redwood Optimize based on trace replay.
- Persistent KV cache warmup: they will pre-populate frequently used prefixes during match windows; request enable cache pre-warm APIs.
- Autoscaling: want strict cap—no autoscale above reserved capacity without explicit approval (cost concern).
- Observability: must expose per-token cost breakdown and token-level tracing for debugging auction latency spikes.

Quotes / verbatim:
- "If we miss bid deadlines because throughput drops, we lose revenue instantly — we need deterministic guarantees, not probabilistic." — VP Eng (A. Patel)
other_comments: POC metrics looked promising: sustained 130k tokens/sec on 2xH100 with batching tuned; next negotiation pivot is SLA legal language and explicit burst accounting. Procurement prefers a 12-month commitment with quarterly review. SE ask: produce a short runbook for failover behavior during burst exhaustion.
